Key Message 1...Increasingly drier conditions return through
Friday.

A vertically-stacked low at the surface and aloft wobbles 
NE'ward from the Long Island and southern New England area to 
the Canadian Maritimes this morning through Friday. Simultaneously,
a ridge at the surface and aloft builds from the western Great 
Lakes and vicinity so that by sunset Friday evening, the surface
ridge axis should become located near Long Island and Lake 
Champlain. Isolated to scattered rain showers associated with 
the low pressure system's weakening warm conveyor belt 
undergoing moist isentropic ascent and convergence/moist ascent
in the low's low-level cyclonic circulation will impact our CWA
from roughly the Genesee River Valley and points to the east
through about 8 AM EDT this morning. The convection will exit 
our CWA slowly later this morning through early evening as the 
low pressure system departs NE'ward. Shower coverage will be 
greatest this afternoon through early evening as weak boundary 
layer destabilization via daytime heating occurs. Isolated 
thunderstorms are possible this afternoon and early evening, 
when the aforementioned low-level convergence/moist ascent may 
release sufficient boundary layer CAPE. Otherwise, fair weather 
is expected through Friday as the aforementioned ridge builds 
from the west and is accompanied by stabilizing subsidence.

Given the projected weather pattern evolution at the surface 
and aloft, weak low-level CAA through tonight is expected to 
transition to weak low-level WAA on the synoptic-scale by 
Friday. Highs should reach the 70's to 80F late this afternoon. 
Considerable clearing of sky, lower humidity at/near the 
surface, and weak surface winds should permit efficient 
radiational cooling and allow lows to reach mainly the 50's to 
lower 60's around daybreak Friday. River valley steam fog is 
expected around daybreak in the Western Southern Tier, Finger 
Lakes, and the Saint Lawrence and Black River Valleys. With the 
departure of the low aloft and its associated cool pool, late 
afternoon highs should recover to seasonable levels (mainly 
upper 70's to mid 80's) on Friday.

Key Message 2...Periodic showers and thunderstorms are expected 
Friday night through this weekend.

The above-mentioned ridge at the surface and aloft should exit
E'ward Friday night as a shortwave trough approaches from the
Upper Midwest and vicinity. Mainly fair weather is expected. 
However, a few showers and thunderstorms are possible over Lake 
Ontario, the Niagara Frontier, and vicinity since moist 
isentropic ascent ahead of the shortwave trough axis may release
sufficient elevated CAPE. Lows should reach mainly the mid 50's
to mid 60's around daybreak Saturday. On Saturday, the 
aforementioned ridge should continue to exit E'ward as the 
shortwave trough axis advances toward the western Great Lakes.
Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms should develop
along the Lake Ontario lake breeze front and especially the Lake
Erie lake breeze front and the Lake Erie/Lake Ontario lake
breeze convergence zone near the Niagara Escarpment Saturday
afternoon and early evening as the boundary layer destabilizes
weakly to moderately via daytime heating and low-level 
warm/moist air advection from the Gulf and southern Gulf Stream.
Periods of heavy rainfall are expected as PWAT values rise to
unusually-high values. Training showers/thunderstorms are
possible along the Lake Erie lake breeze front south and east 
of the lake, where SW'erly and fairly weak mean mid-level flow 
should exhibit a large component parallel to the lake breeze
front. Localized flash flooding may become a concern. Primarily
weak deep-layer bulk shear should curb severe storm potential. 
Late afternoon highs should reach mainly the upper 70's to mid 
80's.

The shortwave trough axis should advance from near the western
Great Lakes to near the NY/New England border Saturday night
through Sunday night. At the surface, a cold front accompanying
the shortwave disturbance should drift SE'ward across our CWA
Saturday night through Sunday evening. Behind the shortwave
trough axis and front, a ridge at the surface and aloft should
build from the Upper Midwest and vicinity through daybreak
Monday. Addtional periods of showers and thunderstorms are 
expected Saturday night through Sunday evening as weak to
moderate instability, including elevated CAPE, is released by
convergence/moist ascent along the front and moist-isentropic
ascent ahead of the shortwave trough axis. Unusually-high PWAT's
within the low-level warm/moist air advection regime from the
Gulf and/or southern Gulf Stream should allow convection to
produce periods of heavy rainfall. SW'erly mean mid-level flow
should exhibit a large component parallel to the synoptic front
and allow convection to train. Thus, localized flash flooding
should remain a concern. Deep-layer bulk shear strengthening to
moderate to strong magnitudes may support stronger storms
